claim: Defects affecting tissues of the anterior segment (AS) of the eye lead to a group of highly debilitating disorders called Anterior Segment Dysgenesis (ASD).
source: Defects affecting tissues of the anterior segment (AS) of the eye lead to a group of highly debilitating disorders called Anterior Segment Dysgenesis (ASD).
evidence: This is a definitional statement establishing the relationship between AS defects and ASD, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Several ciliopathies display conditions of the anterior segment.
source: Interestingly, several ciliopathies display conditions of the AS.
evidence: This statement references established clinical observations about ciliopathies, representing knowledge from the field.

claim: Conditional targeting of Ift88 with Wnt1-Cre ablates primary cilia of neural crest cells.
source: Using conditional targeting of Ift88 with Wnt1-Cre, we show that primary cilia of neural crest cells (NCC), precursors of most AS structures, are indispensable for normal AS development
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach and demonstrates cilia ablation through immunofluorescence and TEM data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Primary cilia of neural crest cells are indispensable for normal AS development.
source: Using conditional targeting of Ift88 with Wnt1-Cre, we show that primary cilia of neural crest cells (NCC), precursors of most AS structures, are indispensable for normal AS development
evidence: This conclusion is supported by the phenotypic data showing ASD conditions in cKO mice presented throughout the manuscript, particularly in Figures 2-3.

claim: Ablation of primary cilia in neural crest cells leads to abnormal corneal dimensions.
source: their ablation leads to ASD conditions including abnormal corneal dimensions, defective iridocorneal angle, reduced anterior chamber volume and corneal neovascularization.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2C demonstrating reduced corneal stroma thickness and corneal diameter in cKO embryos.

claim: Ablation of primary cilia in neural crest cells leads to defective iridocorneal angle.
source: their ablation leads to ASD conditions including abnormal corneal dimensions, defective iridocorneal angle, reduced anterior chamber volume and corneal neovascularization.
evidence: This is demonstrated by histological analysis in Figure 2D showing disorganized iridocorneal angle in cKO embryos.

claim: Ablation of primary cilia in neural crest cells leads to reduced anterior chamber volume.
source: their ablation leads to ASD conditions including abnormal corneal dimensions, defective iridocorneal angle, reduced anterior chamber volume and corneal neovascularization.
evidence: This is shown in histological sections in Figure 2B-D demonstrating a significantly reduced anterior chamber in cKO samples.

claim: Ablation of primary cilia in neural crest cells leads to corneal neovascularization.
source: their ablation leads to ASD conditions including abnormal corneal dimensions, defective iridocorneal angle, reduced anterior chamber volume and corneal neovascularization.
evidence: This is demonstrated by endomucin staining in Figure 7B-G showing abnormal blood vessel spread into cKO corneas.

claim: NCC cilia ablation abolishes hedgehog (Hh) signaling in the periocular mesenchyme (POM).
source: Mechanistically, NCC cilia ablation abolishes hedgehog (Hh) signaling in the periocular mesenchyme (POM) canonically activated by choroid-secreted Indian Hh
evidence: This is demonstrated by Gli1-LacZ reporter staining in Figure 4C showing absence of Hh activity in POM of cKO embryos, and by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4B showing decreased Gli1 and Ptch1 expression.

claim: Hedgehog signaling in the periocular mesenchyme is canonically activated by choroid-secreted Indian Hh.
source: Mechanistically, NCC cilia ablation abolishes hedgehog (Hh) signaling in the periocular mesenchyme (POM) canonically activated by choroid-secreted Indian Hh
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 6A-C showing Ihh expression in the sclera and specifically in choroidal endothelial cells.

claim: NCC cilia ablation reduces proliferation of POM cells surrounding the retinal pigment epithelium.
source: reduces proliferation of POM cells surrounding the retinal pigment epithelium
evidence: This is demonstrated by Ki67 and BrdU staining quantified in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing significantly decreased proliferation in the 0-20 μm POM region adjacent to RPE in cKO embryos.

claim: NCC cilia ablation decreases the expression of Foxc1 and Pitx2.
source: decreases the expression of Foxc1 and Pitx2, two transcription factors identified as major ASD causative genes.
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7A demonstrating significantly reduced Foxc1 and Pitx2 expression in cKO corneas.

claim: Foxc1 and Pitx2 are two transcription factors identified as major ASD causative genes.
source: Foxc1 and Pitx2, two transcription factors identified as major ASD causative genes.
evidence: This represents established knowledge from the ASD literature, as referenced in the Discussion section citing multiple studies (D'haene et al., 2011).

claim: Approximately 50% of ASD patients develop glaucoma that can lead to visual impairment and blindness.
source: Approximately 50% of ASD patients develop glaucoma that can lead to visual impairment and blindness (Cvekl and Tamm, 2004; Ito and Walter, 2014; Ma et al., 2019; Reis and Semina, 2011).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from the literature about ASD patient outcomes.

claim: Most AS structures are derived from neural crest cells (NCC) during development.
source: During development, most AS structures are derived from the neural crest cells (NCC), including the corneal stroma and endothelium, ciliary body muscle and body, iris stroma, and the trabecular meshwork (Gage et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established developmental biology knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Migrating NCC of the periocular mesenchyme begin to invade the AS of the eye between E11.5 and E12.5 during murine development.
source: Migrating NCC of the periocular mesenchyme (POM) begin to invade the AS of the eye between E11.5 and E12.5 during murine development and differentiate into corneal endothelial cells and keratocytes (Pei and Rhodin, 1970; Swamynathan, 2013).
evidence: This is established developmental timing information supported by citations.

claim: At E14.5, all NCC-derived tissues of the POM and the presumptive corneal stroma were ciliated.
source: We observed that at E14.5, all NCC-derived tissues of the POM and the presumptive corneal stroma were ciliated (Figure 1A).
evidence: This observation is directly shown in Figure 1A with Arl13b staining of cilia in Wnt1-Cre;mT/mG embryos.

claim: All stroma keratocytes are ciliated at adulthood in mice.
source: Intravital microscopy revealed that cilia were present in all keratocytes of the corneal stroma of 3-month-old mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by intravital microscopy of Sstr3::GFP mice shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Primary cilia disassemble in adult corneal endothelium at steady state.
source: Our previous studies reported that while primary cilia are present in developing corneal endothelium (also a NCC-derived tissue), they disassemble in adult corneal endothelium at steady state (Blitzer et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a cited finding from previous work by the authors.

claim: In developing eyes, cilia emanated from the cellular surface into the extracellular matrix.
source: TEM showed that in developing eyes, cilia emanated from the cellular surface into the extracellular matrix, whereas cilia of newborn keratocytes appeared to be intracellular or largely invaginated in a long ciliary pocket with their axis parallel to the cell plane (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM images shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Cilia of newborn keratocytes appeared to be intracellular or largely invaginated in a long ciliary pocket with their axis parallel to the cell plane.
source: TEM showed that in developing eyes, cilia emanated from the cellular surface into the extracellular matrix, whereas cilia of newborn keratocytes appeared to be intracellular or largely invaginated in a long ciliary pocket with their axis parallel to the cell plane (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM images shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: The tip of cilia in developing cornea and POM were observed to interact with cellular protrusions of neighboring cells.
source: Interestingly, the tip of cilia in developing cornea and POM were observed to interact with cellular protrusions of neighboring cells (Figure 1C–D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM images shown in Figure 1C-D.

claim: The plasma membrane of cellular protrusions at the contact point with ciliary tips appeared to be highly electron-dense.
source: Moreover, the plasma membrane of these cellular protrusions at the contact point with ciliary tips appeared to be highly electron-dense, suggesting the presence of protein components or modified lipids in this region (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from TEM images shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: The electron-dense plasma membrane at ciliary tip contact points suggests the presence of protein components or modified lipids in this region.
source: Moreover, the plasma membrane of these cellular protrusions at the contact point with ciliary tips appeared to be highly electron-dense, suggesting the presence of protein components or modified lipids in this region (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the electron-dense appearance observed in TEM.

claim: Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx mouse is phenotypically indistinguishable from the null hemizygous Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/-.
source: We generated the Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx mouse (cKO) which was phenotypically indistinguishable from the null hemizygous Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/-.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental generation of mouse lines.

claim: In Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx;mT/mG cKO mice, cilia were absent in most of the POM cells expressing Cre.
source: In Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx;mT/mG cKO mice, cilia were absent in most of the POM cells expressing Cre (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Primary cilia were only observed emanating from basal bodies of control keratocytes but not cKO keratocytes.
source: We confirmed ablation of cilia in keratocyte precursors by TEM and observed the basal body apparatus to reach the apical plasma membrane in both control and cKO corneas, however, primary cilia were only observed emanating from basal bodies of control keratocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by TEM images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx mutant mice died at birth.
source: Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx mutant mice died at birth
evidence: This is a direct observation from the mouse breeding experiments.

claim: E18.5 Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx embryos displayed strong craniofacial defects including increased frontal width, wider frontonasal prominence and increase of the distance between the nasal pits.
source: Wnt1-Cre;Ift88fx/fx mutant mice died at birth and E18.5 embryos displayed strong craniofacial defects including increased frontal width, wider frontonasal prominence and increase of the distance between the nasal pits, consistent with previous studies (Figure 2A) (Tian et al., 2017; Watanabe et al., 2019).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and is consistent with cited previous studies.

claim: At E14.5, the axis of the eyeballs was misaligned facing downward in cKO whereas in control it remained perpendicular to the sagittal plane of the head.
source: At E14.5, a developmental stage preceding the closure of the eyelids, the axis of the eyeballs was misaligned facing downward in cKO whereas, in control it remained perpendicular to the sagittal plane of the head (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The outline of the presumptive iris appeared irregular in cKO while in the control it described a nearly perfect circle at E14.5.
source: Furthermore, the outline of the presumptive iris appeared irregular in cKO while in the control it described a nearly perfect circle (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation shown in Figure 2A.

claim: At E18.5, the developing cornea appeared smaller in cKO than in control.
source: Later in development (E18.5), the irregularities of the iris were exaggerated in cKO and the developing cornea appeared smaller than that of the control, strongly arguing toward severe defects of the AS including a reduced anterior chamber (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2C.

claim: The eye field of cKO embryos at E10.5 and 14.5 appeared indistinguishable from that of the control.
source: The eye field of cKO embryos at E10.5 and 14.5 appeared indistinguishable from that of the control (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is shown in histological sections in Figure 2B.

claim: At E15.5, a significant reduction of the anterior chamber was observed in the cKO samples.
source: In contrast, at E15.5, we observed a significant reduction of the anterior chamber in the cKO samples (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is shown in histological sections in Figure 2B-D.

claim: At E15.5, the cKO mutant was lacking most of the mesenchymal cells condensing at the developing iridocorneal angle between the cornea and the presumptive iris.
source: At this stage, the mutant was lacking most of the mesenchymal cells condensing at the developing iridocorneal angle between the cornea and the presumptive iris that was clearly visible in the control (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is shown in plastic sections in Figure 2D.

claim: Between E16.5 and E18.5, the corneal stroma thickness and the corneal diameter were both significantly reduced in the cKO embryo compared to the control.
source: Between E16.5 and E18.5, the corneal stroma thickness and the corneal diameter were both significantly reduced in the cKO embryo compared to the control (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 2C showing statistically significant differences.

claim: The density of keratocytes was significantly higher in the cKO stroma compared to control at E18.5.
source: Plastic cross sections of the cornea revealed that the density of keratocytes was significantly higher in the cKO stroma compared to control however, the total number of cells in corneal stroma remained unchanged in both genotypes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 2E showing statistically significant differences.

claim: The total number of cells in corneal stroma remained unchanged between cKO and control genotypes at E18.5.
source: Plastic cross sections of the cornea revealed that the density of keratocytes was significantly higher in the cKO stroma compared to control however, the total number of cells in corneal stroma remained unchanged in both genotypes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 2E.

claim: The increased keratocyte density in cKO was attributed to the smaller volume cornea compared to control.
source: The increased keratocyte density was therefore attributed to the smaller volume cornea in cKO embryos compared to control.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing unchanged total cell number but increased density in a smaller cornea.

claim: The unchanged number of keratocytes in the stroma of both genotypes suggests that primary cilium ablation did not impair the NCC migration into the corneal stroma.
source: The unchanged number of keratocytes in the stroma of both genotypes suggests that primary cilium ablation did not impair the NCC migration into the corneal stroma.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing equal total cell numbers in both genotypes.

claim: In control embryos, the amount of extracellular spaces was significantly lower in the posterior than the anterior portion of the corneal stroma.
source: In control embryos, the amount of extracellular spaces was significantly lower in the posterior than the anterior portion of the corneal stroma, defining an antero-posterior gradient of keratocyte density (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 3B showing statistically significant differences.

claim: In control embryos, the size of the extracellular spaces in the posterior part was significantly smaller than in the anterior part.
source: This was mirrored in the stroma in control embryos with the size of the extracellular spaces in the posterior part being significantly smaller than in the anterior part, defining an antero-posterior gradient of the extracellular space size (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 3C showing statistically significant differences.

claim: In cKO embryos, the antero-posterior gradient of the keratocyte density was maintained as in control.
source: In cKO embryos, the antero-posterior gradient of the keratocyte density was maintained as in control, while the average size of extracellular spaces was not (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The amount of extracellular space was significantly reduced in both the anterior and posterior parts of the cKO stroma compared to control.
source: The amount of extracellular space was significantly reduced in both the anterior and posterior parts of the cKO stroma compared to control (Figure 3B–C)
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 3B-C showing statistically significant differences.

claim: The number of cytoplasmic processes was significantly increased in the cKO embryos compared to control.
source: The number of cytoplasmic processes was significantly increased in the cKO embryos compared to control (Figure 3D–E)
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 3E showing statistically significant differences.

claim: At E18.5, the expression of Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4 and Smad7 remained indistinguishable between the cKO and control mice.
source: At E18.5, the expression of Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4 and Smad7 and the percentage of pSmad2/3+ cells in the cornea remained indistinguishable between the cKO and control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The percentage of pSmad2/3+ cells in the cornea remained indistinguishable between the cKO and control mice at E18.5.
source: At E18.5, the expression of Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Smad2, Smad3, Smad4 and Smad7 and the percentage of pSmad2/3+ cells in the cornea remained indistinguishable between the cKO and control mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown by immunostaining quantification in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: NCC from E18.5 cKO mouse showed a significant decrease of Hh target genes including Gli1 and Ptch1 when compared to control NCC.
source: NCC from E18.5 cKO mouse showed a significant decrease of Hh target genes including Gli1 and Ptch1 but not CyclinD when compared to control NCC (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4B with statistical significance indicated.

claim: CyclinD expression was not significantly changed in cKO NCC compared to control at E18.5.
source: NCC from E18.5 cKO mouse showed a significant decrease of Hh target genes including Gli1 and Ptch1 but not CyclinD when compared to control NCC (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Expression of Wnt and Notch pathway target genes remained unchanged between mutant and control NCC at E18.5.
source: In contrast, expression of target genes of the Wnt and Notch pathways, including Axin2, β-catenin, Lef1, Hey1, Hes1 and Maml1 remained unchanged between mutant and control (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: In E12.5 control mice, intense Hh activity was detected in most of the POM, as all cells were strongly LacZ-positive.
source: In E12.5 control mice, we detected intense Hh activity in most of the POM, as all cells were strongly LacZ-positive (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C.

claim: At E14.5 and E18.5, the Hh activity in the POM was greatly decreased with only a subpopulation of POM cells surrounding the RPE layer remaining positive.
source: At E14.5 and E18.5, the Hh activity in the POM was greatly decreased with only a subpopulation of POM cells surrounding the RPE layer remaining positive.
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C.

claim: The layer of Hh responsive cells extended from the optic nerve area to the iridocorneal angle in control embryos.
source: This layer of Hh responsive cells extended from the optic nerve area to the iridocorneal angle in control embryos (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C.

claim: By adulthood, the Hh signaling remained active only in the choroid area, around the optic nerve, and in the ciliary body.
source: By adulthood, the Hh signaling remained active only in the choroid area, around the optic nerve, and in the ciliary body (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In cKO mice, the Hh activity was nearly completely absent in the POM at any developmental stages.
source: In contrast, in cKO mice, the Hh activity was nearly completely absent in the POM at any developmental stages.
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C.

claim: Intense Hh activity was detected in tissues derived from the neuroectoderm including the retina and RPE at all developmental stages in both mutant and control mice.
source: In both mutant and control mice, we detected intense Hh activity in tissues derived from the neuroectoderm including the retina and RPE at all developmental stages (Figure 4C) (Wang et al., 2002).
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: No Hh activity was detected in the cornea of cKO or control mice between E12.5 and E18.5.
source: Interestingly, no Hh activity was detected in the cornea of cKO or control mice between E12.5 and E18.5 despite the presence of cilia in keratocyte precursors throughout development (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is shown by Gli1-LacZ staining in Figure 4C.

claim: At E14.5, cell proliferation was significantly decreased in the POM close to the RPE layer (0–20 µm) in the cKO mutants compared to control.
source: At E14.5, cell proliferation was significantly decreased in the POM close to the RPE layer (0–20 µm) in the cKO mutants compared to control (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 showing statistically significant differences.

claim: Proliferation rates remained unchanged in the outer region of the POM (20–50 µm) and in the cornea where Hh was normally not activated.
source: In contrast, proliferation rates remained unchanged in the outer region of the POM (20–50 µm) and in the cornea where Hh was normally not activated (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of Ihh was significantly higher than Dhh and Shh in the sclera including the RPE layer, but not in the cornea at E18.5.
source: We observed that expression of Ihh was significantly higher than Dhh and Shh in the sclera including the RPE layer, but not in the cornea (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 6A.

claim: Shh but not Dhh or Ihh was expressed in the isolated neural retina where NCC are excluded.
source: As expected, we found that Shh but not Dhh or Ihh was expressed in the isolated neural retina where NCC are excluded (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 6A.

claim: At E18.5, among the non-NCC, Ihh was significantly more expressed by the choroidal endothelial cells than Dhh and Shh.
source: At E18.5, among the non-NCC, Ihh was significantly more expressed by the choroidal endothelial cells than Dhh and Shh (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data from sorted cells in Figure 6C with statistical significance indicated.

claim: At E14.5 and P0, all cells of the POM were ciliated.
source: At E14.5 and P0, all cells of the POM were ciliated (Figure 6E)
evidence: This is shown by confocal microscopy of whole-mount scleras in Figure 6E.

claim: At E14.5, SMO accumulated in primary cilia on the inner cell layers of the POM surrounding the RPE (0–18 μm).
source: At E14.5, we observed an accumulation of SMO in primary cilia on the inner cell layers of the POM surrounding the RPE (0–18 μm), consistent with the Hh activity detected in these cell layers (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown by SMO immunostaining in Figure 6E-F.

claim: SMO was not detected in the primary cilium of cells of the peripheral POM (>18 μm from the RPE) at E14.5.
source: In contrast, we did not detect SMO in the primary cilium of cells of the peripheral POM (>18 μm from the RPE) (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This is shown by SMO immunostaining in Figure 6E-F.

claim: At P0, SMO was undetectable in primary cilia of NCC in the entire POM.
source: At P0, SMO was undetectable in primary cilia of NCC in the entire POM (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This is shown by SMO immunostaining in Figure 6E-F.

claim: When eyeballs from P0 mice were treated with a SMO agonist (SAG), SMO accumulated in cilia of POM cells.
source: However, when eyeballs from P0 mice were treated with a SMO agonist (SAG), SMO accumulated in cilia of POM cells (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This is shown by SMO immunostaining after SAG treatment in Figure 6E-F.

claim: POM cells of the P0 sclera were still able to activate Hh signaling upon ligand stimulation.
source: This implies that POM cells of the P0 sclera were still able to activate Hh signaling upon ligand stimulation, suggesting that the decreased Hh activity in the POM during ocular development is controlled by the diffusion of the Hh ligand Ihh in the POM.
evidence: This is inferred from the SAG stimulation experiment showing SMO accumulation in cilia upon agonist treatment.

claim: The decreased Hh activity in the POM during ocular development is controlled by the diffusion of the Hh ligand Ihh in the POM.
source: This implies that POM cells of the P0 sclera were still able to activate Hh signaling upon ligand stimulation, suggesting that the decreased Hh activity in the POM during ocular development is controlled by the diffusion of the Hh ligand Ihh in the POM.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the observation that cells retain the ability to respond to Hh but show decreased activity in vivo.

claim: Expression of Foxc1 and Pitx2 was significantly decreased in corneas of cKO embryos compared to controls at E18.5.
source: RT-qPCR analysis revealed that expression of Foxc1 and Pitx2 was significantly decreased in corneas of cKO embryos compared to controls, while Pax6 expression remained unchanged (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7A with statistical significance indicated.

claim: Pax6 expression remained unchanged between cKO and control corneas at E18.5.
source: RT-qPCR analysis revealed that expression of Foxc1 and Pitx2 was significantly decreased in corneas of cKO embryos compared to controls, while Pax6 expression remained unchanged (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is shown by RT-qPCR data in Figure 7A.

claim: Abnormal spread of blood vessels was detected into the corneas of E18.5 cKO mutant embryos.
source: Abnormal spread of blood vessels was detected into the corneas of E18.5 cKO mutant embryos (Figure 7B–C)
evidence: This is shown by endomucin staining in Figure 7B-C.

claim: Blood vessels covered about 8% of the total corneal area in E18.5 cKO embryos.
source: where vessels covered about 8% of the total corneal area (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 7D.

claim: The average area occupied by blood vessels in microscope fields selected at the corneal periphery occupied ~30% of the total area in the cKO but only ~4% in the control.
source: The average area occupied by blood vessels in microscope fields selected at the corneal periphery occupied ~30% of the total area in the cKO but only ~4% in the control (Figure 7E–F).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 7F.

claim: Peripheral blood vessels of the control were present only in superficial layers of the sclera-cornea interface on both sides of the major arterial circle (~20% of the thickness).
source: In addition, while peripheral blood vessels of the control were present only in superficial layers of the sclera-cornea interface on both sides of the major arterial circle (~20% of the thickness), those of the mutant invaded the lower layers of both, the sclera (~50% of the thickness) and the cornea (~80% of the thickness).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 7G.

claim: Blood vessels of the mutant invaded the lower layers of both the sclera (~50% of the thickness) and the cornea (~80% of the thickness).
source: In addition, while peripheral blood vessels of the control were present only in superficial layers of the sclera-cornea interface on both sides of the major arterial circle (~20% of the thickness), those of the mutant invaded the lower layers of both, the sclera (~50% of the thickness) and the cornea (~80% of the thickness).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 7G.

claim: Corneas of both control and cKO embryos were innervated during development.
source: During development, corneas of both control and cKO embryos were innervated (Figure 8A)
evidence: This is shown by TUJ1 staining in Figure 8A.

claim: At E13.5, the number of nerve bundles detected in the cKO eye was significantly lower than that of the control.
source: however, at E13.5, the number of nerve bundles detected in the cKO eye was significantly lower than that of the control (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 8B showing statistically significant differences.

claim: Abnormally long nerve projections across the cornea were observed in cKO embryos at E13.5 while nerves were only visible at the periphery of the control cornea.
source: Moreover, abnormally long nerve projections across the cornea were observed in cKO embryos while nerves were only visible at the periphery of the control cornea (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 8A.

claim: At E18.5, corneas of both genotypes were fully innervated.
source: At E18.5, corneas of both genotypes were fully innervated (Figure 8A), including the corneal epithelium (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown by TUJ1 staining in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The corneal nerve density was significantly higher in the cKO embryos at E18.5.
source: However, the corneal nerve density was significantly higher in the cKO embryos (Figure 8C)
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 8C showing statistically significant differences.

claim: The nerves in cKO corneas were less organized centripetally compared to the control at E18.5.
source: and the nerves in cKO corneas were less organized centripetally compared to the control (Figure 8D–E).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 8E showing statistically significant differences in angle measurements.

claim: The average angle θ formed by the major nerve branches with the radius of the cornea was significantly larger in cKO embryos compared to controls at E18.5.
source: The average angle θ formed by the major nerve branches with the radius of the cornea was significantly larger in cKO embryos compared to controls (Figure 8D–E).
evidence: This is quantified in Figure 8E showing statistically significant differences.

claim: Primary cilium ablation in the NCC impaired the early corneal innervation and the centripetal migration of the sensory nerves.
source: These data suggest that primary cilium ablation in the NCC impaired the early corneal innervation and the centripetal migration of the sensory nerves.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nerve bundle and organization data presented in Figure 8.

claim: Patients affected by Meckel syndrome present AS abnormalities including microphthalmos/anophthalmos, aniridia, cryptophthalmos, sclerocornea, abnormal corneal thickness, corneal neovascularization, and abnormal iridocorneal angle.
source: Patients affected by Meckel syndrome, a severe ciliopathy, present AS abnormalities including microphthalmos/anophthalmos, aniridia, cryptophthalmos, sclerocornea, abnormal corneal thickness, corneal neovascularization, and abnormal iridocorneal angle (MacRae et al., 1972).
evidence: This is cited information from the literature about Meckel syndrome.

claim: Oral-facial-digital syndrome has been reported to include several cases of microphthalmia.
source: Oral-facial-digital syndrome has recently been reported to include several cases of microphthalmia (Abuhamda and Elsous, 2018; Cortés et al., 2016)
evidence: This is cited information from the literature.

claim: A patient affected by Joubert syndrome has been described with corneal opacity.
source: and a patient affected by Joubert syndrome has been described with corneal opacity (Zaki et al., 2011).

claim: Glaucoma and cataract are conditions associated with Bardet-Biedl and Lowe syndromes.
